title: The urgent account warning — question explanation
learningObjective: Identify urgency, unexpected requests and mismatched context in a suspicious message
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A message says your learning-platform account will be disabled in 20 minutes unless you sign in through its embedded link. You were not expecting an account notice.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Identify urgency, unexpected requests and mismatched context in a suspicious message
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Open the platform using a saved bookmark or typed known address, then check notices; report the message if suspicious. Independently navigate to the known service instead of trusting the embedded link, and report suspicious mail through the approved channel.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Replying engages the sender and does not independently establish identity. Option C: Wider forwarding can spread malicious links and expose recipients; use the approved reporting route. Option D: This follows the message’s pressure and may disclose credentials to a look-alike site.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Do not open the embedded link. Navigate independently to the service and report the message using the organization’s phishing-report process. Pause when a message creates urgency; verify through a channel you already trust.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Pause when a message creates urgency; verify through a channel you already trust.
